speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have chronic joint pain; to begin my evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and which specific joints are affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest in the hips and knees is classic for osteoarthritis; however, the involvement of the left great toe raises concern for gout or inflammatory arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Serum Uric Acid, Rheumatoid Factor, and ESR/CRP. Also, do you notice any morning stiffness lasting longer than 30 minutes?
